04 · Read & review

The transcript

Submit all six answers to unlock the transcript. You can then listen and read together.

Back at the hotel, Emma replayed the meeting from her notes. Reid had admitted withholding information; he had not said what it was. That distinction frustrated her, but it was the only responsible account of the conversation.

She called Sarah and read the crucial sentences aloud. Sarah asked whether Reid had consented to attribution. Emma said he had agreed that she could report his acknowledgement of an incomplete follow-up, subject to giving him a chance to check the wording for factual accuracy. She would not give him editorial control.

"You have something," Sarah said. "Not enough to publish the whole story, but something that deserves careful checking."

Emma sent Reid a short written summary of what she understood him to have said. She asked him to identify factual inaccuracies, not to rewrite the questions. Then she submitted the narrower records request.

An email arrived from Calum. The college had found an archived account entry corresponding to the scholarship period. It showed a payment, but not on the date he had been told to expect it, and not for the full amount stated in his original award letter. The college had not yet confirmed whether later adjustments existed. Emma asked permission to obtain a certified extract before drawing conclusions.

For a moment she considered the two lines of enquiry together: a delayed scholarship payment and a police officer's incomplete note. They concerned the same trust and the same town, across 2010 and 2011. That was not enough to make them one conspiracy. She drew a line between them on her page and wrote possible connection — unproven.

At dusk she walked to the river. She thought about the family who had waited for answers in 2011, about the people whose names had appeared in articles they had never wanted written, and about the difference between protecting someone's privacy and deciding on their behalf what the public should know.

Her phone vibrated. Reid had replied to her summary.

Your account of what I said is accurate. I am prepared to explain my conduct to the appropriate authorities. I cannot tell you Claire Morrison's current whereabouts. I do not know them.

Emma read the last sentence twice. It did not answer whether he had known where Claire was in 2011. She would ask that another day, when the record was clearer.

For now, she saved the message, dated it and returned to her hotel. The next person she needed to speak to was James Morrison. If anyone had earned the right to distrust her questions, it was Claire's brother.
